newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian Democrats claim big win in local poll.
newsitem.headline: Albanian Democrats claim big win in local poll.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha on Monday, announcing his Democratic Party swept the board in local polls at the weekend, said the result underscored its triumph at national level five months ago.
"Albanian voters chose the best alternative and candidates. Albanians confirmed the May 26 (general election) results once again and I am very proud of that," Berisha told reporters.
The opposition Socialists, reformed heirs to the communists, were less flattering in their assessment of Sunday's vote.
"The essence about these elections is that they were not free and fair according to us," secretary general Rexhep Mejdani told a news conference.
Albanian general elections in May and June ended in controversy when most opposition parties, including the Socialists, withdrew alleging the ballot was rigged.
The Democrats took 122 seats in the 140-member parliament while the Socialists refused to take up the 10 that they won.
On Monday the Democrats said their preliminary results for the local polls showed they had gained more than 61 percent of city halls, including Tirana, and 58 percent of commune seats.
The Socialists had won just six percent of city halls and commune seats, down from over 50 percent in 1992, the Democrats said.
Official results are due in the next few days.
Mejdani said Sunday's vote marked a step backwards for Albanian democracy and accused the Democrats of manipulating the ballot out of sight of the legions of Western observers.
The Council of Europe, which coordinated monitoring, has yet to present its report on the elections but it has said initial findings suggest there were no serious incidents.

Claus Francke, the German head of the European Democratic Union monitors team which watched some 120 polling stations, said Sunday's elections were free and fair and there had been no irregularities at all.
But the Socialists stood by their claims that armed bands had intimidated the electorate and Democrat supporters had tampered with the count.
The two main parties even disagreed on the turnout, with the Socialists arguing participation was well below the 75 percent the Demcrats claimed.
Berisha renewed his call on the opposition to take up its seats in parliament so that it could play a role in Albania's democratic development.
